interpretation: The two extant sister species alone do not polarize the colour change: C and W are equally parsimonious at the Arenicola MRCA.
Coloured MRCA requires one C->W loss on the brevicaule lineage.
White MRCA requires one W->C regain on the irumtiense lineage.
With the published coloured-rich Nipponocirsium sister context, equal-cost parsimony selects Arenicola MRCA=C; this is topology-conditioned, not a molecular regain/loss demonstration.
Tests the white-loss history explicitly; delta is relative to the unconstrained sister-context optimum.
Tests the irumtiense-regain history explicitly. A positive delta means it needs extra topology-level changes under the current sister context, but it remains a live biological hypothesis.
Conditions the Arenicola+Nipponocirsium parent on a coloured state.
White deep-root sensitivity. Under this external prior the preferred Arenicola MRCA can switch to W, demonstrating why independent root/branch-length evidence matters.
